title: Capstone: Govern the Data Plane
subtitle: Tag-driven masking + row filters, Immuta-style
content:
🎯 Mission

Govern a finance analytics warehouse: tag PII columns, write one global masking policy with an auditor exception, one row-filter policy (analysts see only their department), and a guardrail (training-complete required). Prove fail-closed behavior on a mis-scoped table. No Immuta tenant? Alternate track: OPA data-filtering compile-to-SQL (Lesson 12) + Postgres RLS/masking views — same artifacts (taxonomy, transcripts, parity diff against native SQL), no console required.

Time model (honest): 480 min across sessions — M1 taxonomy + masking (150) → M2 row filters + guardrail (150) → M3 lockout + evidence (180).

📦 Definition of Done

  • Tag taxonomy documented (PII, PII.SSN depth demo showing deeper-tag-wins; same-depth tie-break noted).
  • Global mask-by-tag with AUDIT exception; numeric-column fallback demonstrated (NULL, not hash-string).
  • Row filter via @columnTagged (never hard-coded names); two-filter AND behavior shown; OR-via-single-policy shown.
  • Guardrail + grant merge demonstrated (per-policy Always Required vs Share Responsibility + guardrail).
  • Lockout demo run staged / domain-first (never directly on prod scope): mis-scoped global on a tag-less table returns zero rows, with the fix (re-tag) recorded.
  • Native-parity artifact: generated/synced native code (warehouse RLS/masking) reviewed against the Immuta/PlainID-authored policy for drift.

📊 Rubric (14/20 to pass) — one artifact per row

Submit: taxonomy.md, policy exports, transcripts/*.md (markdown: command + output per demo step), remediation.log, native-parity.diff. Score each row 0 (absent), partial (present but unchecked), or full per the check. Points: partial = 1 pt on every row (including 2-pt row 3); full = listed pts. Max 20, pass at 14.

#Artifact (pts)PartialFull
1Taxonomy + depth demo transcript (3)Tags applied, no conflict demoTranscript shows PII vs PII.SSN resolution AND states the same-depth tie-break
2Masking per-role transcript (3)Masked, exception untestedTranscript shows analyst NULL vs auditor hash vs owner raw on the same table
3Numeric fallback proof (2)Claimed in proseTranscript shows a numeric column returning typed NULL (not a hash-string)
4Row-filter AND/OR demo (3)Filters exist, composition unexplainedTranscript shows two filters ANDing plus OR-inside-one-policy
5Guardrail merge demo (3)Guardrail named, merge untestedTranscript shows Always Required ANDing vs Share Responsibility ORing against the same table
6Staged lockout + re-tag log (3)Lockout shown without remediationStaged-scope lockout transcript AND remediation.log with the re-tag fix
7Native-parity diff (3)Generated code attached unreviewednative-parity.diff reviewed line-by-line against the authored policy, drift noted or clean
🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Preview every masking verdict in the simulator before implementing. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: PII and PII.SSN masking policies both match a column. Which applies?

options.text: PII.SSN (deeper tag wins as more specific)
PII (shallower wins)
Neither — they cancel out
A random one

questions.explanation: Docs-verified specificity rule — your capstone must demonstrate global-mask resolution by tag depth, not just claim it (Lesson 17).

questions.question: Why must the row filter use @columnTagged instead of a literal column name?

options.text: Literal names break on tables lacking the column → lockout; tags adapt per table
Tags run faster
Column names are illegal
No reason — purely cosmetic

questions.explanation: The lockout lesson: globals must be written against tags so heterogeneous tables each resolve sensibly.

questions.question: Analysts need rows for dept A OR dept B. How?

options.text: One policy containing the OR (separate row policies AND together)
Two separate row policies (they OR automatically)
Delete one department's data
Row filters cannot express OR

questions.explanation: Verified composition: row policies AND; OR lives inside a single policy. Getting this backwards silently over-restricts (or under-).

questions.question: Training-complete guardrail + manager-grant both apply. New hire without training but with manager approval?

options.text: Denied — guardrails are always required on top of any grant
Allowed — the grant overrides
Allowed — guardrails apply only to contractors
Error — conflicting policies halt evaluation

questions.explanation: Guardrail AND semantics: delegation-safe by design. Grants widen, guardrails bound.

questions.question: Your mis-scoped global returns zero rows on the demo table. How do you present this?

options.text: As the lockout success case: fail-closed evidence + the re-tag fix, logged
Hide it — zero rows looks like failure
Switch to fail-open so rows appear
Present it as a warehouse bug, re-scope silently

questions.explanation: Lockout is the data plane proving it fails closed. Documented + remediated lockout is rubric points, not embarrassment.

questions.question: Analysts in two departments need each other's aggregates but never each other's rows. Design?

options.text: Row filter denies rows plus a separate aggregate view under its own policy — never weaken the filter
Weaken the row filter to allow both
Share logins across departments
Export CSVs by email

questions.explanation: Aggregates are a different access shape with different inference risk. Separate view, separate policy, separate review.

questions.question: The training guardrail blocks new hires because the HR feed lags 48 hours. Fix that preserves safety?

options.text: Time-boxed provisional grant with expiry and manager approval, auto-revoked on feed sync
Drop the guardrail permanently
Permanent exception for all new hires
Allow all new hires during onboarding

questions.explanation: Stale feeds need bounded exceptions, not removed guardrails. Expiry plus approval plus auto-revoke keeps the invariant.

questions.question: A new PII subtype appears (device IDs). Steps?

options.text: Extend the taxonomy (PII.Device), tag, verify deeper-tag-wins, add a regression test
Ignore it until audit finds it
Rename every existing tag
Mask every column manually

questions.explanation: Taxonomies are living governance. New data classes flow through tag → policy → test, the same pipeline as day one.
